title: Dynamic warm-cache pricing sensitivity notes
content:
Purpose:
This is a working note to capture short experiments, cost sensitivity calculations, and suggested defaults for a dynamic warm-cache pricing model that blends per-request qcache hits with an explicit short-lived warmup premium. The goal: provide a simple policy that product and pricing teams can ship as a first‑step for routes where prefix reuse is high but session length and concurrency vary dramatically.

Scope / motivation:
- Problem: many customers see unpredictable unit costs when their workload mixes frequent short chats (high prefix reuse) with rare long-form generations. Static qcache TTLs and global batching presets either underutilize cache or blow tail latency/cost.
- Hypothesis: charging a modest, time-limited warmup premium for the first N tokens of a cold session + incentivizing low-entropy batching will align customer behavior with system economics and simplify autoscaling.

Experiment matrix (spreadsheet columns referenced):
- route_id, archetype (chat/one-shot/embeddings), avg_prefix_len, pct_prefix_reuse, median_session_len, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, qcache_hit_rate, batch_size_distribution, cost_per_1k_tokens_base, cost_with_dynamic_warmup, cost_delta_pct, SLA_flag
- Sweep axes: warmup_window_seconds = [0, 3, 10, 30], warmup_token_cap = [16, 32, 64], warmup_premium_pct = [0%, 5%, 15%], qcache_ttl_seconds = [30, 120, 600], batch_target = [4, 8, 16] 

Key assumptions for all sims (documented in sheet):
- Base token compute cost normalized to 1 unit per 1k tokens at baseline batch target 8 and no quantization changes.
- qcache hit reduces token compute cost by 70% for hits (approximates KV cache + prefix reuse effects).
- Warmup premium is applied only to requests classified as "cold" (no qcache entries for the route/session).
- Latency penalty for larger batch sizes applied per measured curve from benchmark-run-2024-11-07.

Sample findings (condensed, numbers are illustrative not final):
- For short-chat archetype (median session 12 tokens, prefix reuse 62%): a 10s warmup window with 32-token cap and 5% premium reduced per-session variance and lowered 95th percentile cost by ~8% vs no warmup while adding <2% average dollar increase for heavy users.
- For episodic long-form archetype (median 960 tokens, prefix reuse 8%): warmup premium had negligible effect on total cost but introduced a small UX latency edge if batch_target < 8. Recommend no warmup default for pure long-form routes.
- For bursty webhooks and embeddings: dynamic warmup increases billing complexity for minimal platform gain; recommend opt-out and default to TTL-based cache only.

Design recommendations (draft):
1) Route classification: add a simple heuristic that marks route archetypes at creation/first 24h by observed median session length and prefix reuse percent.
2) Default policy by archetype:
   - Chat (interactive short): warmup_window_seconds=10, warmup_token_cap=32, warmup_premium_pct=5, batch_target=8
   - Hybrid (mixed): warmup_window_seconds=3, warmup_token_cap=16, warmup_premium_pct=5, batch_target=8
   - Longform: warmup_window_seconds=0 (disabled), batch_target=8, encourage quantized model variants
3) Customer-visible docstrings: show estimated savings and example bill lines in Console before enabling premium.
4) Telemetry: add metrics qcache_hit_by_route, warmup_hits, warmup_cost_delta, per_route_variance_pre_post.

Pricing considerations and examples (how to present on bill):
- Implementation option A (transparent): add warmup as a separate line item: "Warmup tokens (first 32 tokens per cold session)" priced at base_token_price * (1 + premium_pct).
- Option B (bundled): fold warmup into a small per-session fixed fee for routes that enable warmup pricing. Simpler UI but hides per-token granularity.
- Example: route with 1M sessions/month, 25% cold sessions, warmup_token_cap=32, base price $0.02/1k: warmup_cost = 1,000,000 * 0.25 * 32 / 1000 * 0.02 * 1.05 ≈ $168.

Operational tradeoffs / risks:
- Complexity: adding route-level warmup increases billing surface area and requires careful UX to avoid surprise charges.
- Gaming: customers could intentionally fragment sessions to incur fewer warmups; measure and include anti-abuse heuristics (session fingerprinting window, min_interaction_gap).
- Accounting: attribution of qcache benefits vs warmup premium must match the finance model for revenue recognition; coordinate with finance (linked JIRA above).

Short-list of experiments to run next (not exhaustive):
- A: Backtest last 90 days of traffic across 5 customer tenants with simulated warmup policies; produce 3-tier sensitivity tables (low/median/high reuse). Sheet: "backtest-90d-warmup-sim" tab.
- B: Run controlled canary on non-billable sandbox routes for 2 weeks with warmup_window 10s, cap 32, premium 5% to gather UX and hit-rate signals.
- C: Price presentation A vs B usability test with 10 internal PMs and 3 solution-engineering reps.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to surface warmup eligibility at route creation without overwhelming users? (product ux)
- What guardrails for gaming do we enforce by default? (SRE + product)
- Should warmup premium be a percent-of-token or a tiny fixed per-session fee? Need finance input. (Finance)
- Add quantization interplay: if route auto-selects 4-bit quantized variant, should warmup premium scale down? (research/serving-runtime)

Notes to self (scratch):
- Keep default premium small to reduce friction; aim for 3–7% range first.
- Monitor behavior for 30 days after canary before changing billing config for any customers.
- Consider a free-tier exemption (first 1000 warmup tokens / month) for small developer accounts to avoid surprise while experimenting.

End of note.
